div.div:
optimizer::optimize_both(working) (optimize() wraps it and keeps only the model input and the crop). Two steps, then a control.
1 Colour balance: Levels, once per image. lo = 0.68 percentile, hi = 99.32 percentile (lowest lo / highest hi of the 3 channels), gamma = 1 + lo/(255-lo) - (255-hi)/hi (0.01-9.99), one 256-entry table. Identity table: used as is.
2 Trim, on the balanced image: 16 border samples (4 per edge, at 0/25/50/75%) give the backdrop colour range (min/max per channel). Gaps closed with a 2x2 window. Box around the product, squared to its largest side, grown by max(10 px, 10% of that side); the square is slid inside the frame. Crop.
3 Control, trim 2 (recheck_box): the same trim run again on trim 1's box. Recorded only when a side moved by more than TRIM_RECHECK_TOLERANCE_PX (2). The model never sees it; core::framing reads both boxes.
Nothing left = Err: the file stays in INPUT.

div.div:
R1 · center_and_stretch
Square = larger axis need: extent × (1 + 4.2% per free side: 8.4% with two free sides, 4.2% with one, none if bled at both ends). Bled edge pinned; slack to the free sides. CentreContent (core::framing) cuts from the content box instead; Prepared::letterbox set → extend.rs.
Rows, then columns. Per line: product band (silhouette grown 20 working px) copied; background beside it stretched (none at the product, most at the border, x^R1_STRETCH_CURVE_POWER); the rest invented from nearby background, clamped to its colour range. A side with no background → inpaint::fill_segment. Empty mask / no legal square → R3

div.div:
extend.rs · Part C (center_and_stretch/extend.rs)
Re-frame a trimmed textured scene to a square, without R1's background stretch.
Wired: R1 calls reframe_to_square when Prepared::letterbox is set.
1 square_crop_preserving(subject, w, h) — crop a square that keeps the whole subject; None if it cannot.
2 seam_carve_to_square(src, target) — grow each axis by minimum-energy seam insertion; None when the cheapest seams cost more than R1_SEAM_CARVE_MAX_SEAM_ENERGY.
3 white_pad(src) — last resort: centre on a white square.
reframe_to_square tries 1, 2, 3 in that order.

text.tspan: w, h) — crop a square that keeps
the whole subject; None if it cannot.

div.div:
core::framing — after the one model run: decide(frame, trim 1, trim 2, edges touched, mask box, texture)
Bars on one axis (cuts of similar width), subject on one edge, smooth content → Crop: bars dropped, R1 frames the content (EIX kept)
Same, but two edges or busy content → Centre: padded, content centred
Square ring round a smaller subject → Peel: deepen_peel, crop, edge check again
Anything else → Keep. One log line says why.

text.tspan: core::framing — after the one model run: decide(frame,
trim 1, trim 2, edges touched, mask box, texture)
Bars on one axis (cuts of similar width), subject on one
edge, smooth content → Crop: bars dropped, R1 frames
Same, but two edges or busy content → Centre: padded,
Square ring round a smaller subject → Peel:
Anything else → Keep. One log line says why.
